newsitem.title: USA: FTC plans impartial review of Boeing merger.
newsitem.headline: FTC plans impartial review of Boeing merger.

text.p: The Federal Trade Commission will review the merger of Boeing Corp. and McDonnell Douglas Corp. without regard to politics or trade policy, FTC Chairman Robert Pitofsky said Friday.
Pitofsky was responding to a letter sent Thursday to President Clinton from Washington State Sen. Slade Gorton.
Gorton, a Republican, said he was concerned about the position of the European Union on the proposed merger of Boeing, which is based in his home state, with McDonnell Douglas.
Gorton also noted the merger should be reviewed in the United States "strictly on its merits with full regard to due process, and not be allowed to become a political or trade issue."
Pitofsky said that was exactly how the five-member commmission and its staff intended to proceed.

"Sen. Gorton and his colleagues want to ensure that review of the Boeing transaction be non-political, not connected with trade and focused on the antitrust issue," Pitofsky said in a brief interview. "We're pleased with that and we're going to do our best to do it exactly that way."
But Pitofsky, who met recently with the top European Union competition official during a visit to Washington, declined to comment on the international aspect of the letter.

Gorton charged that Karel Van Miert, who heads competition policy in the EU, has made public statements "about his negative views of the proposed (Boeing) transaction (that) are inapopropriate, prejudicial and do grave harm to the due process that is both the legal right of the involved parties and the foundation of fair and impartial antitrust review by regulatory authorities."
Van Miert has expressed concerns that the merger would unfairly narrow competition with the European commercial airline consortium, Airbus Industrie.
The EU will decide on the Boeing merger by the end of July. The EU was closed Friday for a holiday and there was no immediate comment from its headquarters in Brussels.
